caption_hook: Missouri sits on old seafloors, a lead treasure chest and the stumps of ancient volcanoes.

layers.name: PEORIA LOESS
layers.hook: Dust blown off the ice age
layers.what: When the glaciers melted, winds whipped silt off the river floodplains and piled it into steep bluffs along the Missouri River, in places dozens of feet thick.
layers.bonus: The Loess Hills of northwest Missouri are some of the few big loess bluffs on Earth.

layers.name: BETHANY FALLS LIMESTONE
layers.hook: A city built on a shallow sea
layers.what: Kansas City sits on layers of limestone and shale laid down in warm seas that flooded in and out. This hard limestone bed is quarried under the city.
layers.bonus: SubTropolis, a giant business park, fills the mined-out caves inside it.

layers.name: BURLINGTON LIMESTONE
layers.hook: A rock made of sea lilies
layers.what: A clear tropical sea covered Missouri, carpeted with crinoids, animals that look like flowers on stalks. Their broken stems piled up into thick white limestone.
layers.bonus: The crinoid is Missouri's official state fossil.

layers.name: GASCONADE DOLOMITE
layers.hook: Why Missouri is the Cave State
layers.what: This Ozark bedrock dissolves slowly in rainwater, riddling the hills with sinkholes, springs and caves. Missouri has more than 7,000 known caves.
layers.bonus: At Ha Ha Tonka, a collapsed cave left a natural bridge and a sinkhole lined with cliffs.

layers.name: BONNETERRE DOLOMITE
layers.what: An ancient reef around the Ozark islands later filled with lead and zinc ore from hot underground fluids. Missouri has led the nation in lead for over a century.
layers.bonus: Galena, the shiny lead ore, is Missouri's state mineral.

layers.name: ST. FRANCOIS GRANITE
layers.what: The St. Francois Mountains are the worn-down stumps of volcanoes and granite that cooled underground 1.5 billion years ago. They poked above the seas as islands.
layers.bonus: At Elephant Rocks, the granite weathered into a herd of giant pink boulders.
